brief: Implement `init()` and `forward()`: a 32-bit float tensor of shape $[B,S,D]$ passes through $L$ layers of causal self-attention and feed-forward network and comes out the same shape. The statement gives every formula, the weight layout, the grader and a sample to check against.

ul: Inputs, expected outputs, baseline times and a checker for all 8 shapes come with the task, the same inputs used for grading; the baseline code is not public.
Every element must be finite and within 0.005 or 2% of the expected value; internal precision and method are free.
Only the CUDA Runtime, the C++ standard library and header-only libraries that need no extra linking; no linked libraries such as cuBLAS, and no Driver API.
All computation from $x$ to $y$ happens on the GPU inside `forward()`; tensors may not be copied back to the CPU for computing.
Shape 4 ($S=100000$) must be split into batches of at most 1 second each; a single kernel running over about 2 seconds resets the driver.

points: **Matrix work on the GPU**: matrix multiplication, softmax and layer normalization are all hand-written; kernel throughput sets the ceiling.
**Precision and tolerance**: internal precision is free to choose, but results must stay within tolerance.

**Memory and platform limits**: very long sequences cannot hold an $S\times S$ intermediate, and work must be split into batches; running it all at once can reset the driver or even crash the machine.
**Tuning per shape**: the 8 shapes range from ten thousand short sequences to a single sequence of 100,000 tokens, and tiling, layout and precision can be chosen per shape.
scoring: **Scored per input**: each shape gets a speedup s = baseline time ÷ solution time, looked up on a log-scale anchor table, 0 at 0.2× or less and full marks from 16×; the task score is the average of the 8 inputs, so long-running shapes carry no extra weight.

**Timed side by side**: the baseline is a general optimized solution written by the task setter; it and the solution each run 3 times in the same evaluation under the same conditions, taking the median.
**Tolerance is the gate**: an input outside tolerance or failing to run scores 0.
**Rules come first**: a compile failure or a broken rule, such as computing tensors on the CPU or calling the Driver API, scores 0 for the whole task.
